description:
Publish source as an agent: a SOUL.md describing who it is, a valet.yaml declaring the skills, connectors, channels, and configuration it runs with, and any supporting files. Use it when the user wants an agent on Valet that answers on a channel or runs on a schedule. Read the organization's requirements with get_skill governance before calling. A policy set to block refuses a publish that fails it, and the answer names what to fix; a monitor policy only records findings, which get_evaluation lists.

files carries the agent in the call, from any client. push: {id, commit} publishes a commit you pushed after create_push, with the sha its recipe prints; use it when you can run git with network access or changed a clone of the agent's source. A push built on a main that has since moved is merged onto it as a deploy is, and one whose tree is already deployed answers no_changes. Pass files or push, not both.

Unlike a website's or an app's, an agent's valet.yaml is yours: Valet validates it rather than writing it, and refuses one the agent rules reject. An organization connector or channel the manifest names is attached for you, but not a Slack channel, which a person sets up, or one whose attach failed. When the manifest names one that is missing or not attached, or a skill that does not resolve, nothing deploys and pending lists each with the tool that sets it up; call again with the same files after.

Publishing changes an agent that exists: create it first with create_service (kind: agent), then publish to its name. Publishing replaces the agent's source with these files, so read get_source first when the agent is not yours. An agent deploy finishes before this call returns: the answer carries the release version, and get_service reports whether the agent is running and what it holds. In an organization with release policies, the answer may carry evaluation instead of a version: the release is built and waits for its policies, and get_evaluation with wait_seconds 20 follows it. Requires connecting a Valet account.

discard_draft.description: Set true to discard an open draft on this agent that another session left. Omit to be told about it instead. Not used with push.

files.description: The agent's files. Give this or push, not both. valet.yaml and SOUL.md at the root are required.

path.description: Path of the file relative to the agent root, such as docs/guide.md.

idempotency_key.description: An opaque key of your choosing. Repeating a call with the same key returns the first call's result instead of deploying a second release. Use a new key for new files: a repeated key returns the earlier result even when the files changed. A call that deployed nothing gives its key back.

name.description: The agent's name. The agent must exist: create it first with create_service. Publishing to it replaces its source.

org_name.description: The Valet organization to publish into. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

push.description: Publish a Git push instead of files: the id create_push returned and the commit you pushed to its branch. Use it when you can run git with network access, because it sends only what changed. Pass files or push, not both; every other argument keeps its meaning.

commit.description: The full sha of the commit you pushed to the push's branch. The recipe create_push returned prints it.

name: publish_agent

evaluation.description: The release evaluation. Without version, the release is built and waits for its policies: follow it with get_evaluation. With version, the release is live and this is its monitor-only evaluation. Absent when the release has none.

deploy.description: What deploy did with the release: 'waiting' for the policies, 'live', or the code of the refusal. Absent when deploy has not decided.

deploy_message.description: The refusal's message when deploy refused the release. Absent otherwise.

id.description: ID of the release evaluation. Pass it to get_evaluation as evaluation_id.

monitor_findings.description: Count of findings monitor policies reported on a live release. They never block it; get_evaluation shows each. Absent when zero.

monitor_running.description: Names of monitor policies still pending or running on a live release. They never block it. Absent when none are.

status.description: Status of the evaluation across its release policies. get_evaluation lists the per-policy results.

no_changes.description: True when the pushed tree is what the agent already runs, so nothing deployed. Absent otherwise.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

pending.description: What the organization must set up before the agent deploys. Nothing deployed. Set each up with its tool, then call publish_agent again with the same files. Absent when the publish went through.

attach.description: Connectors and channels the organization has but the agent does not hold, because publishing could not attach them: a Slack channel, which a person sets up, or one whose attach failed. Attach each to the agent.

catalog.description: The catalog entry the manifest names for it.

kind.description: Whether the dependency is a 'connector' or a 'channel'.

install.description: Connectors and channels the manifest names that the organization has no instance of. Create each from its catalog entry.

catalog.description: The catalog entry the manifest names for it.

kind.description: Whether the dependency is a 'connector' or a 'channel'.

skills.description: Skill references in the manifest that do not resolve.

version.description: Version number of the release the publish activated. Absent when nothing deployed: the call is pending (see pending), the release waits for its policies (see evaluation), or nothing changed.

title: Publish an agent
